monthly.summary: Kaguguta Agrifarm recorded 40.8mm of rain in August 2026, roughly 0.9 times the long-term August average of around 48mm and in the near-average range. Rain fell on 12 days, with 6 days above 1mm, and the final dekad accounted for 28.3mm of the monthly total. Rainfall was concentrated at the end of the month, with 19.0mm falling between 29 and 31 August, including the month's heaviest day, 30 August, at 15.4mm. Heavy rainfall also fell on 22 August (8.1mm) and 5 August (5.0mm), and no day exceeded 20mm. Regionally, the Indian Ocean Dipole remained neutral through August, though the WMO and ICPAC forecast a positive phase developing alongside a strengthening El Niño, which ICPAC said normally enhances October to December rainfall and pointed to wetter-than-normal short rains for the region.

Kaguguta Agrifarm recorded 122.8mm of rain in September 2026, roughly 3.5 times the long-term September average of around 35mm and well above normal for the month. Rain fell on 23 days, with five days exceeding 10mm and three exceeding 20mm; the heaviest were 27.7mm on 11 Sep, 24.1mm on 18 Sep and 20.2mm on 27 Sep. A large share of the total came in a short burst, with 58.7mm falling between 17 and 21 September, including 42.3mm in the three days from 18 to 20 September. The second dekad was the wettest, at 74.5mm, compared with 10.6mm in the first and 37.7mm in the third. Regionally, forecasters had pointed to a positive Indian Ocean Dipole alongside a developing El Niño, a combination that ICPAC said normally enhances rainfall in the Greater Horn of Africa and that it expected to bring a wetter-than-normal October to December season.

daily_narrative: KILIFI, Kenya, 6 October 2026 – The Kaguguta Agrifarm weather station recorded 0.56 mm of rain on 5 October, ending a three-day dry spell that began on 2 October. The station has logged 1.7 mm so far in the first dekad of October, all of it falling on 1 and 5 October, with the monthly total at the same figure. Rainfall in early October is well below the late-September pace, when 20.16 mm fell on 27 September and 16.80 mm and 15.00 mm fell on 20 and 21 September respectively. No ECMWF ensemble forecast was available at the time of reporting.
dekadal_narrative: Rainfall for the dekad totalled 37.7 mm over 8 rainy days, which was more than Sep-D1 at 10.6 mm but less than Sep-D2 at 74.5 mm. Two days accounted for most of the total: 20.2 mm fell on 27 September, with an instantaneous peak rate of 53 mm/h at 08:42 and a maximum 1-hour accumulation of 5.0 mm, and 15.0 mm fell on 21 September, together making up about 93% of the dekad. The remaining days each recorded 1.1 mm or less, and 25 and 26 September were dry. The forecast for the next dekad points to a wetter period, with a total of 165.1 mm and the heaviest falls expected from 12 to 14 October, peaking at 38.6 mm on 13 October. A positive Indian Ocean Dipole is developing, with the Bureau of Meteorology's weekly index at +0.76°C for the week ending 27 September, above the +0.4°C threshold for a third consecutive week, and this phase tends to enhance short-rains rainfall over East Africa; KMSA's October-December outlook accordingly favours above-average rainfall for Kilifi.
